data.content_ref: inline:The target's proposed evidence — low inter-rater variance plus causal-language transcripts — fails to distinguish genuine reliability from mere compliance, because a checklist can be algorithmically rigid enough to force both low variance AND rote-but-uniform causal justifications. The target itself concedes this flaw in its own counterconditions (the 'algorithmically rigid' case), then fails to resolve it: it offers no evidence criterion that separates a panel that converged on a shared causal understanding from a panel that converged because the checklist dictated the same causal narrative. Thus under the target's own standard, a compliant panel mechanically reproducing checklist-linked causal language would be misclassified as a genuine reliability gain within a single evaluation.
